title: [Hyprland] Closing Alacritty/Gnome terminal window with an open display-popup crashes the tmux server
body:
### Issue description

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/520d4da9-dfd0-4a16-b4bf-f863547b28b0

It crashes the same way with a tmux compiled from the source, with or without my configuration.

> [!WARNING]
> I also tried the same with kitty, and it seems to work fine.

### Required information

Please provide the following information:

* tmux version (`tmux -V`).
  - tmux next-3.6
* Platform (`uname -sp`).
  - Linux unknown
* Terminal
  - alacritty 0.14.0 (22a44757)
* $TERM inside and outside of tmux (`echo $TERM`).
  - alacritty
  - tmux-256color
* Logs from tmux (`tmux kill-server; tmux -vv new; tmux -vv new`).
Build from source, no configuration, same steps as shown in the video.
  - [tmux-client-32675.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18320628/tmux-client-32675.log)
  - [tmux-client-32852.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18320630/tmux-client-32852.log)
  - [tmux-out-32677.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18320631/tmux-out-32677.log)
  - [tmux-server-32677.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18320632/tmux-server-32677.log)

comments.body:
I can't reproduce this and there is nothing useful in the log. Does tmux leave a core file?

If not, try to attach gdb to the tmux server and reproduce, so start tmux and then in another terminal do this:
~~~~
gdb `which tmux` `tmux display -p '#{pid}'`
~~~~
Then reproduce and after it crashes go back to gdb and do `bt` to see the backtrace.
